title: The 10 Billion Milestone: The Path to Humanity's Peak
subtitle: How the world population grew from 1 billion in 1804 and why it will stabilize around 2084.

slides.title: From Dawn to 1 Billion
slides.text: For almost all of human history, the total world population remained below a few hundred million. It was not until 1804, with advances in sanitation and agriculture, that humanity reached its first 1 billion people.

slides.title: The 20th Century Explosion
slides.text: It took over a century to reach 2 billion (1927), but only 47 years to double to 4 billion in 1974. Antibiotics, vaccines, and the Green Revolution drastically lowered child mortality worldwide.

slides.title: Crossing 8 Billion in 2022
slides.text: Humanity officially crossed 8 billion in late 2022. While population continues growing by ~71 million people annually, the global growth rate has plummeted from 2.1% in the 1960s to below 0.86% today.

slides.title: The Fertility Transition
slides.text: Half of all nations now have fertility rates below the replacement level (2.1 births per woman). Global fertility has dropped from 5.0 in 1950 to 2.25 in 2024, driving unprecedented demographic stabilization.

slides.title: Humanity's Peak at 10.3 Billion
slides.text: According to the UN 2024 medium variant projections, world population will peak at approximately 10.3 billion people in the 2080s, before gradually stabilizing and gently contracting by 2100.

title: The Great Clean Energy Transition
subtitle: How solar, wind, and nuclear are transforming global electricity grids.

slides.title: Breaking the 30% Barrier
slides.text: In 2024, renewable and nuclear energy produced over 30% of global electricity for the first time, marking a decisive tipping point in world decarbonization.

slides.title: The Exponential Rise of Solar
slides.text: Solar photovoltaic capacity expanded faster than any other electricity source in human history, adding over 400 GW in a single calendar year.

slides.title: Regional Front-Runners
slides.text: Brazil generates nearly 90% of its electricity from hydro, wind, and biomass. France achieves 92% clean electricity through its nuclear and renewable mix.

slides.title: The Decarbonization Horizon
slides.text: Under current international commitments, global clean electricity share is projected to reach 60% by 2035, driven by battery grid storage and offshore wind.

title: The Urban Century: Rise of the Megacities
subtitle: How 4.5 billion people came to live in cities and where urbanization heads next.

slides.title: The Majority Urban World
slides.text: In 2007, humanity crossed an irreversible milestone: for the first time, more people lived in urban areas than in rural villages.

slides.title: The Age of 30+ Megacities
slides.text: Metropolises with over 10 million inhabitants grew from just 3 in 1975 (Tokyo, New York, Mexico City) to 34 megacities today, concentrated heavily across Asia and Africa.

slides.title: Tokyo to Delhi: Changing Ranks
slides.text: While Tokyo holds the current #1 spot at 37.4 million, its population is stabilizing. Delhi is projected to surpass Tokyo before 2030 to become the most populous agglomeration on Earth.

slides.title: Towards 68% Urban by 2050
slides.text: By 2050, more than two out of every three people on Earth will live in urban centers, demanding unprecedented smart infrastructure, mass transit, and green architecture.
